chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: 'It Was a Lover and His Lass' and the Shakespeare idea
summary: Claude's Shakespeare setting, sound effects in the studio, and later Shakespeare albums.

blocks.x: It has a lot of tongue and cheek quality --

Yes. In the studio there was a prop there for sound effects. And there was a door sitting over there, and by this time, there was no room for anymore bird whistles, so for Dave to earn his money, he had to go shut the door. And I'd say, 'Goodnight,' for no good reason at all, except, you know, to keep it in the song.
That's an entirely different version from the one you recorded in 1971?
Right.
With Dick Hyman (unintelligible) on your Shakespeare album.
Right. You know, there's been a lot of renditions of 'Lover, Come Back, Come Home.' But Dick had evidently heard some of the things -- and I didn't even know Dick at that time.
But he liked the idea. Later on, I made an album in which we repeated some of the things I did and it was the first time he had ever accompanied a singer.
That was '55.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
That's right.
Flow Gently, Sweet Rhythm.
Yeah, right.
Okay.

So he got the idea of doing this Shakespeare catalog. And he mentioned to me that he actually had me in mind when he did it. And, of course, the album -- his album, the one that was made with him, they're just lightly swung. I mean, he did a very good job of keeping the -- what I would say as the Elizabethan flavor, but with a beat. Since we're on that -- talking about that one -- the --
In this particular case, he uses a calypso --
Yeah, he uses a calypso beat. And, of course, 'Dark Eyes' -- we repeated 'Dark Eyes' for the Vocalion label, because --
No, no.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

I mean for Victor -- we repeated it, yeah. We repeated it on the Victor label -- I don't know why we repeated it -- but I liked the Victor rendition better, because by the time we recorded it, I had be doing it quite -- well like every night in the club. And I felt a little bit more comfortable with the arrangement. I feel that it's more relaxed than the early one. In fact, I was just learning when I recorded (it for) Vocalion, I had seen it for the first time and trying to tangle up with those Russian lyrics. It wasn't easy either. I still wonder if, you know, if it's Russian or just phonetic. But I liked the tune and I liked the arrangement. I think Claude did a very good arrangement of it. And I felt very good about it. It's a sad song and I like it.
(inaudible) asked you to sing it with a southern accent of (inaudible).
We'll talk about that
